svg.title: The common seating translation exists by two finite avoidance steps. First choose a translation placing the main positions at distance five buffer scales from the coarse cell boundaries; the total excluded intervals fit because |I|10af < ab. Then shift by at most one intermediate cell scale to place the exterior positions at distance three fine insertion scales from their cell boundaries, using |J|6an < al. The second shift consumes at most two of the five main buffer scales, leaving the required three. The nested cell periods divide the larger periods. Replica displacements are integer multiples of these periods, so they leave every boundary residue and hence all margins unchanged. Actual torus separations follow from the Euclidean ones for sufficiently large periods: the physical distance is at most twice the mesh times the wrapped lattice separation. Subsequent embedding multiplies lattice separations by the mesh ratio, proving the required inequalities at every finer cutoff.
